sentiment.rationale: The document reports strong backward-looking results (record EPS, 20.5% comparable sales growth, $9 billion market share gain) but explicitly withdraws guidance for Fiscal 2021 due to 'continued uncertainty' regarding COVID-19. The forward-looking signal is flat: management expresses confidence in the business model but provides no formal guidance raise or reduction, and the lack of guidance combined with cautious language about the outlook anchors the score at neutral.

summary.revenue: Total revenue of $28.3 billion in Q4 2020, up 21.1% year-over-year. Full-year revenue of $93.6 billion, up 19.8%.
summary.eps: Q4 2020 GAAP EPS from continuing operations of $2.73 (up 67.7% from $1.63 in Q4 2019); Adjusted EPS of $2.67 (up 58.2% from $1.69). Full-year GAAP EPS of $8.64 (up 36.3% from $6.34); Adjusted EPS of $9.42 (up 47.4% from $6.39).
summary.guidance: The company is not providing sales and EPS guidance for Fiscal 2021 and beyond due to continued uncertainty from COVID-19.
summary.margin: Q4 2020 gross margin rate 26.8% vs 26.3% in 2019; operating income margin rate 6.5% vs 5.1% in 2019. Full-year gross margin rate 28.4% vs 28.9% in 2019; full-year operating income margin rate 7.0% vs 6.0% in 2019.
key_risks: Continued uncertainty from COVID-19 impacting consumer shopping patterns and the outlook for fiscal 2021.
Higher digital fulfillment and supply chain costs partially offsetting gross margin benefits.
Unfavorable category sales mix and higher supply chain and fulfillment costs from channel mix affecting full-year gross margin rate.
key_opportunities: Continued market share gains across all five core merchandising categories.
Strong growth in same-day services (Order Pick Up, Drive Up, Shipt) up 212% in Q4, led by more than 500% growth in Drive Up.
Digital sales grew by nearly $10 billion in 2020, driven by 235% growth in same-day services.
More than 95% of Q4 sales fulfilled by stores, demonstrating the strength of the store network as a fulfillment hub.
